ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The line segments $AB$ and $CD$ are on the same straight line, with $M$ and $N$ being the midpoints of line segments $AB$ and $CD$, respectively. It is known that $AB=6\,cm$ and $CD=8\,cm$. When the points $A$ and $C$ coincide, what is the length of $MN$ in $cm$?
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The line segments $AB$ and $CD$ are on the same straight line, with $M$ and $N$ being the midpoints of line segments $AB$ and $CD$, respectively. It is known that $AB=6\,cm$ and $CD=8\,cm$. When the points $A$ and $C$ coincide, what is the length of $MN$ in $cm$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Solution: Since $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of line segments $AB$ and $CD$ respectively, and $AB=6\,cm$, $CD=8\,cm$, with points $A$ and $C$ coinciding,\\ therefore, $AM=3\,cm$, $AN=4\,cm$,\\ hence $MN=AN-AM=\boxed{1\,cm}$;

method.method_draft: Use the shared-endpoint midpoint-gap rule. From the image, read that when A and C coincide, the two segments AB and CD start at the same point and lie on the same ray, with CD longer than AB. From the text, read AB=6 cm and CD=8 cm, and that M and N are the midpoints. Because the segments share the same starting point, the distance from the common endpoint to each midpoint is half the segment length. Thus the separation between the midpoints is half the difference of the whole lengths: MN=(CD-AB)/2=(8-6)/2=1 cm.
